tools.name: search
tools.description:
Finds the tools of the servers below by running JavaScript: write an async arrow function, such as async () => { ... }. It runs in a sandbox with no network or file access. What it returns is structuredContent.result, exactly as returned; the text content holds only what it wrote with console.log (cut at about 24000 characters) or the error it threw. Return only what is needed.

In the code:
- codemode.servers(): Promise<{ id: string, description: string, upstream: boolean }[]>
- codemode.groups(server: string): Promise<string[]>, the groups a large server is split into (empty when it is not)
- codemode.tools(server?: string, group?: string): Promise<{ id: string, description: string, inputSchema: object }[]>, every tool when called with no server (the tools of an upstream are in it once it was started, and those of a server built from its OpenAPI document once they were built for its host, so call codemode.tools(server) for a server whose tools are missing), the tools of one server or one of its groups, or, given the start of a tool id instead of a server (codemode.tools("git:gitlab:api/v4/projects/{id}/merge_requests")), the tools whose ids start with it

Example:
async () => {
  const tools = await codemode.tools();
  return tools.filter((tool) => /branch/.test(tool.id)).map(({ id, description }) => ({ id, description }));
}

Servers:
- security:bitwarden: Bitwarden password manager through its own MCP server (github.com/bitwarden/mcp-server), cloned on first use into ~/.usemcpkit/repos/security/bitwarden, built there and run locally: vault items, folders, attachments, Send, password and TOTP tools. Needs git, Node.js and npm on PATH, the Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) for the vault tools, and a vault unlocked with its `unlock` tool (a native password dialog; BW_SESSION, BW_CLIENT_ID and BW_CLIENT_SECRET from the client's env are passed along when set). It reads and changes real credentials, so allow only the tools you trust.
- productivity:clickup: ClickUp REST API (v2 and v3): tasks, checklists, comments and custom fields, the Workspace hierarchy (spaces, folders, lists, views), time tracking, goals, users and guests, chat, docs, webhooks and audit logs. Tools are named after their endpoint, '<path>:<method>' (api/v2/task/{task_id}:get). The v2 endpoints call the Workspace id `team_id`; list the Workspaces with api/v2/team:get.
- orgs/jetbrains:clion: CLion through the MCP server built into the IDE (2025.2 or later, switched on under Settings → Tools → MCP Server), reached on the local port the running IDE picked, which usemcpkit reads from the IDE's own log. The tools are the IDE's: reading, creating and searching project files, code problems and linting, refactorings, run configurations and builds, the terminal, version control, and whatever the installed plugins add. They act on the projects open in the IDE and need it to be running.
- cloud:cloudflare: The Cloudflare API through Cloudflare's own remote MCP server (github.com/cloudflare/mcp, mcp.cloudflare.com), in code mode: search the OpenAPI spec and run API calls from JavaScript, so every product (Workers, KV, R2, D1, Pages, DNS, firewall, load balancers, Access and more) is reachable through a few tools, plus Cloudflare documentation search and whoami. `execute` can change or delete anything the token allows, so give the token only the permissions you want the AI to have.
- orgs/atlassian:confluence: Confluence REST API of Confluence Cloud (REST v2 and v1) or of the Data Center release the host runs: pages, blog posts, spaces, attachments, comments, labels, properties, users and groups, permissions and administration. Tools are named after their endpoint, '<path>:<method>' (wiki/api/v2/pages/{id}:get on Cloud, rest/api/content/{id}:get on Data Center).
- orgs/jetbrains:datagrip: DataGrip through the MCP server built into the IDE (2025.2 or later, switched on under Settings → Tools → MCP Server), reached on the local port the running IDE picked, which usemcpkit reads from the IDE's own log. The tools are the IDE's: reading, creating and searching project files, code problems and linting, refactorings, run configurations and builds, the terminal, version control, and whatever the installed plugins add. They act on the projects open in the IDE and need it to be running.
- orgs/jetbrains:dataspell: DataSpell through the MCP server built into the IDE (2025.2 or later, switched on under Settings → Tools → MCP Server), reached on the local port the running IDE picked, which usemcpkit reads from the IDE's own log. The tools are the IDE's: reading, creating and searching project files, code problems and linting, refactorings, run configurations and builds, the terminal, version control, and whatever the installed plugins add. They act on the projects open in the IDE and need it to be running.
- communication:discord: Discord HTTP API v10, called as a bot: channels, messages, reactions, threads and pins, guilds (members, roles, bans, emojis, stickers, scheduled events, auto moderation, audit logs), users and DMs, application commands, webhooks, invites and lobbies. Tools are named after their endpoint, '<path>:<method>' (channels/{channel_id}/messages:post). Ids are snowflakes passed as strings; list the bot's guilds with users/@me/guilds:get.
- design:figma: Figma REST API: files and their nodes, rendered images and image fills, versions, comments and reactions, dev resources, published components, component sets, styles and variables, library analytics, teams' projects and folders, webhooks and the current user. Tools are named after their endpoint, '<path>:<method>' (v1/files/{file_key}/nodes:get). A file key is the part after /design/ in a Figma link, and a node id looks like 1:2 (a link carries it as node-id=1-2). v1/files/{file_key}:get returns the whole document and can be enormous: prefer v1/files/{file_key}/nodes:get with ids, or pass depth. Variables need an Enterprise plan; operations that need an OAuth app or an organization token are not included.
- git:github: GitHub REST API of github.com or of the GitHub Enterprise Server version the host runs: repositories, issues and pull requests, Actions, security, organizations, users, apps, Copilot and meta endpoints. Tools are named after their endpoint, '<path>:<method>' (repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls:get), and grouped by the path's first segment.
- git:gitlab: GitLab REST API of gitlab.com or of the self-managed release the host runs: projects, issues and merge requests, CI/CD, packages, security, groups, users, administration, AI and meta endpoints. Tools are named after their endpoint, '<path>:<method>' (api/v4/projects/{id}/merge_requests:get).
- orgs/jetbrains:goland: GoLand through the MCP server built into the IDE (2025.2 or later, switched on under Settings → Tools → MCP Server), reached on the local port the running IDE picked, which usemcpkit reads from the IDE's own log. The tools are the IDE's: reading, creating and searching project files, code problems and linting, refactorings, run configurations and builds, the terminal, version control, and whatever the installed plugins add. They act on the projects open in the IDE and need it to be running.
- orgs/jetbrains:intellij: IntelliJ IDEA through the MCP server built into the IDE (2025.2 or later, switched on under Settings → Tools → MCP Server), reached on the local port the running IDE picked, which usemcpkit reads from the IDE's own log. The tools are the IDE's: reading, creating and searching project files, code problems and linting, refactorings, run configurations and builds, the terminal, version control, and whatever the installed plugins add. They act on the projects open in the IDE and need it to be running.
- orgs/atlassian:jira: Jira REST API of Jira Cloud or of the Data Center release the host runs: issues, projects, users, workflows, fields, dashboards and filters, administration and Jira Software boards and sprints. Tools are named after their endpoint, '<path>:<method>' (rest/api/2/issue/{issueIdOrKey}:get, rest/agile/1.0/board:get); the /rest/api/2 endpoints take plain-text fields.
- communication:medium: Medium's API (api.medium.com/v1), which Medium has archived and no longer supports: it needs an integration token you already have, since Medium stopped issuing new ones. Get the authenticated user (me:get), list their publications and a publication's contributors, publish posts as HTML or Markdown to the profile or a publication (as a draft, unlisted or public), and upload an image. The API cannot read, edit or delete posts. Tools are named after their endpoint, '<path>:<method>'. users/{authorId}/posts:post publishes under the token owner's name, so prefer publishStatus draft.
- automation:n8n: n8n of an n8n Cloud or self-hosted instance, through two APIs that share the instance host. The public REST API (API key): workflows (create, update, publish, activate, archive, transfer, history, tags), executions (list, read, retry, stop), evaluation test runs, credentials and credential type policies, data tables with their columns and rows, projects with their folders, members and variables, users, roles and role mapping rules, instance settings (LDAP, SSO, log streaming, OpenTelemetry, security and node type policies), the security audit, community packages, source control, insights and environment promotions; deprecated operations are not included, which tools work depends on the instance's plan and version and on the API key's scopes, and enterprise features answer 403 without a license. And n8n's own instance-level MCP server (n8n 1.120.0 or later, MCP access turned on under Settings → Instance-level MCP), signed in with one click through n8n's own OAuth: search and run, test, build, update, publish and archive the workflows enabled for MCP, search nodes and validate workflow code, read executions, manage data tables, projects and folders, and on instances that have them agents, skills and credential descriptions; its tools appear once the server was opened with codemode.tools and depend on the instance's version, license and settings and on the permissions granted at sign-in. The REST tools are named after their endpoint, '<path>:<method>' (workflows/{id}:get) and sign in with the API key; the MCP ones are named '<group>:<resource>:<action>' and sign in with their own OAuth or an MCP access token.
- cloud:ngrok: ngrok through ngrok's own remote MCP server (ngrok.com/docs/mcp-server, mcp.ngrok.com): the account, team and access tokens, cloud endpoints and their Traffic Policy, agents, Traffic Inspector requests and connections, reserved domains and TCP addresses, TLS certificates, IP policies, vaults and secrets, log exports, AI Gateway (access configs and keys, providers, virtual models, firewall policies, usage) and the ngrok documentation. Tools that create, change or delete act with your role and the scopes you approved.
- orgs/jetbrains:phpstorm: PhpStorm through the MCP server built into the IDE (2025.2 or later, switched on under Settings → Tools → MCP Server), reached on the local port the running IDE picked, which usemcpkit reads from the IDE's own log. The tools are the IDE's: reading, creating and searching project files, code problems and linting, refactorings, run configurations and builds, the terminal, version control, and whatever the installed plugins add. They act on the projects open in the IDE and need it to be running.
- api:postman: Postman through Postman's own remote MCP server (github.com/postmanlabs/postman-mcp-server, mcp.postman.com) in its Full mode: workspaces, collections with their folders, requests, responses, comments, forks and pull requests, environments, mock servers, monitors, specs, the API catalog, governance rules, SDKs, teams and search. Tools that create, change or delete act with the API key's permissions.
- orgs/jetbrains:pycharm: PyCharm through the MCP server built into the IDE (2025.2 or later, switched on under Settings → Tools → MCP Server), reached on the local port the running IDE picked, which usemcpkit reads from the IDE's own log. - communication:reddit: Reddit's OAuth API (read-only): a subreddit's posts, a post with its comment tree, search for posts and subreddits, subreddit info and rules, user profiles and their posts and comments. Tools are named after their endpoint, '<path>:<method>' (r/{subreddit}/{sort}:get). Posts and comments are identified by fullnames (t3_<id>, t1_<id>); listings page with `after` set to the last item's `name`.
